passages.text: “This is what the Lord GOD says: ‘The gate of the inner court that faces east must be kept shut during the six days of work, but on the Sabbath day and on the day of the New Moon it shall be opened.
passages.sermon:
The Lord GOD speaks.
He gives a command.
There is a gate in the inner court.
This gate faces east.
Keep this gate shut for six days of work.
Open this gate on the Sabbath day.
Open this gate on the day of the New Moon.
passages.original: כֹּֽה־ אָמַר֮ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִה֒ שַׁ֜עַר הֶחָצֵ֤ר הַפְּנִימִית֙ הַפֹּנֶ֣ה קָדִ֔ים יִהְיֶ֣ה סָג֔וּר שֵׁ֖שֶׁת יְמֵ֣י הַֽמַּעֲשֶׂ֑ה וּבְי֤וֹם הַשַּׁבָּת֙ יִפָּתֵ֔חַ וּבְי֥וֹם הַחֹ֖דֶשׁ יִפָּתֵֽחַ׃

passages.text: The prince is to enter from the outside through the portico of the gateway and stand by the gatepost, while the priests sacrifice his burnt offerings and peace offerings. He is to bow in worship at the threshold of the gate and then depart, but the gate must not be shut until evening.
passages.sermon:
The prince enters from outside.
He comes through the portico of the gateway.
He stands by the gatepost.
The priests offer his burnt offerings.
The priests offer his peace offerings.
The prince bows in worship at the threshold of the gate.
Then the prince leaves.
The gate remains open until evening.
No one shuts the gate before evening.
passages.original: וּבָ֣א הַנָּשִׂ֡יא דֶּרֶךְ֩ אוּלָ֨ם הַשַּׁ֜עַר מִח֗וּץ וְעָמַד֙ עַל־ מְזוּזַ֣ת הַשַּׁ֔עַר וְעָשׂ֣וּ הַכֹּהֲנִ֗ים אֶת־ עֽוֹלָתוֹ֙ וְאֶת־ שְׁלָמָ֔יו וְהִֽשְׁתַּחֲוָ֛ה עַל־ מִפְתַּ֥ן הַשַּׁ֖עַר וְיָצָ֑א וְהַשַּׁ֥עַר לֹֽא־ יִסָּגֵ֖ר עַד־ הָעָֽרֶב׃

passages.text: On the Sabbaths and New Moons the people of the land are also to bow in worship before the LORD at the entrance to that gateway.
passages.sermon:
The people of the land must bow in worship before the LORD.
They must do this at the entrance to that gateway.
They must do this on the Sabbaths.
They must do this on the days of the New Moon.
passages.original: וְהִשְׁתַּחֲו֣וּ עַם־ הָאָ֗רֶץ פֶּ֚תַח הַשַּׁ֣עַר הַה֔וּא בַּשַּׁבָּת֖וֹת וּבֶחֳדָשִׁ֑ים לִפְנֵ֖י יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: The burnt offering that the prince presents to the LORD on the Sabbath day shall be six unblemished male lambs and an unblemished ram.
passages.sermon:
The prince is the leader of the people.
The prince brings a burnt offering to the LORD.
He does this on the Sabbath day.
He brings six male lambs.
Each lamb must be unblemished.
He also brings one ram.
The ram must be unblemished.
passages.original: וְהָ֣עֹלָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־ יַקְרִ֥ב הַנָּשִׂ֖יא לַֽיהוָ֑ה בְּי֣וֹם הַשַּׁבָּ֗ת שִׁשָּׁ֧ה כְבָשִׂ֛ים תְּמִימִ֖ם וְאַ֥יִל תָּמִֽים׃

passages.text: The grain offering with the ram shall be one ephah, and the grain offering with the lambs shall be as much as he is able, along with a hin of oil per ephah.
passages.sermon:
The prince brings a grain offering with the ram.
He gives one ephah of grain with the ram.
He brings a grain offering with the lambs.
He gives as much grain with the lambs as he is able.
He adds a hin of oil for each ephah of grain.
passages.original: וּמִנְחָה֙ אֵיפָ֣ה לָאַ֔יִל וְלַכְּבָשִׂ֥ים מִנְחָ֖ה מַתַּ֣ת יָד֑וֹ וְשֶׁ֖מֶן הִ֥ין לָאֵיפָֽה׃

passages.text: On the day of the New Moon he shall offer a young, unblemished bull, six lambs, and a ram without blemish.
passages.sermon:
The prince leads the offerings to the LORD.
He does this on the day of the New Moon.
He brings a young bull.
The bull must have no blemish.
He brings six lambs.
The lambs must have no blemish.
He brings a ram.
The ram must have no blemish.
passages.original: וּבְי֣וֹם הַחֹ֔דֶשׁ פַּ֥ר בֶּן־ בָּקָ֖ר תְּמִימִ֑ם וְשֵׁ֧שֶׁת כְּבָשִׂ֛ם וָאַ֖יִל תְּמִימִ֥ם יִהְיֽוּ׃

passages.text: He is to provide a grain offering of an ephah with the bull, an ephah with the ram, and as much as he is able with the lambs, along with a hin of oil per ephah.
passages.sermon:
The prince must bring a grain offering with each animal.
He must give one ephah of grain with the bull.
He must give one ephah of grain with the ram.
He must give as much grain as he is able with the lambs.
He must add a hin of oil for every ephah of grain.
passages.original: וְאֵיפָ֨ה לַפָּ֜ר וְאֵיפָ֤ה לָאַ֙יִל֙ יַעֲשֶׂ֣ה מִנְחָ֔ה וְלַ֨כְּבָשִׂ֔ים כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר תַּשִּׂ֖יג יָד֑וֹ וְשֶׁ֖מֶן הִ֥ין לָאֵיפָֽה׃

passages.text: When the prince enters, he shall go in through the portico of the gateway, and he shall go out the same way.
passages.sermon:
The prince is the leader of the people.
The prince enters the temple area.
He enters through the portico of the gateway.
He leaves by the same way he entered.
passages.original: וּבְב֖וֹא הַנָּשִׂ֑יא דֶּ֣רֶךְ אוּלָ֤ם הַשַּׁ֙עַר֙ יָב֔וֹא וּבְדַרְכּ֖וֹ יֵצֵֽא׃

passages.text: When the people of the land come before the LORD at the appointed feasts, whoever enters by the north gate to worship must go out by the south gate, and whoever enters by the south gate must go out by the north gate. No one is to return through the gate by which he entered, but each must go out by the opposite gate.
passages.sermon:
The people of the land come before the LORD at the appointed feasts.
Some people enter by the north gate to worship.
These people must go out by the south gate.
Other people enter by the south gate.
These people must go out by the north gate.
No one may return through the gate by which he entered.
Each person must go out by the opposite gate.
passages.original: וּבְב֨וֹא עַם־ הָאָ֜רֶץ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָה֮ בַּמּֽוֹעֲדִים֒ הַבָּ֡א דֶּרֶךְ־ שַׁ֨עַר צָפ֜וֹן לְהִֽשְׁתַּחֲוֺ֗ת יֵצֵא֙ דֶּרֶךְ־ שַׁ֣עַר נֶ֔גֶב וְהַבָּא֙ דֶּרֶךְ־ שַׁ֣עַר נֶ֔גֶב יֵצֵ֖א דֶּרֶךְ־ שַׁ֣עַר צָפ֑וֹנָה לֹ֣א יָשׁ֗וּב דֶּ֤רֶךְ הַשַּׁ֙עַר֙ אֲשֶׁר־ בָּ֣א ב֔וֹ כִּ֥י נִכְח֖וֹ יֵצְאוּ׃

passages.text: When the people enter, the prince shall go in with them, and when they leave, he shall leave.
passages.sermon:
The prince is a leader among the people.
The people enter together.
The prince enters with the people.
The people leave together.
The prince leaves with the people.
passages.original: וְֽהַנָּשִׂ֑יא בְּתוֹכָ֤ם בְּבוֹאָם֙ יָב֔וֹא וּבְצֵאתָ֖ם יֵצֵֽאוּ׃

passages.text: At the festivals and appointed feasts, the grain offering shall be an ephah with a bull, an ephah with a ram, and as much as one is able to give with the lambs, along with a hin of oil per ephah.
passages.sermon:
God gave instructions for offerings at the temple.
At the festivals, the people must bring grain offerings.
At the appointed feasts, the people must also bring grain offerings.
With each bull, the offering is one ephah of grain.
With each ram, the offering is one ephah of grain.
With each lamb, the offering is as much grain as a person is able to give.
With every ephah of grain, the offering must include one hin of oil.
passages.original: וּבַחַגִּ֣ים וּבַמּוֹעֲדִ֗ים תִּהְיֶ֤ה הַמִּנְחָה֙ אֵיפָ֤ה לַפָּר֙ וְאֵיפָ֣ה לָאַ֔יִל וְלַכְּבָשִׂ֖ים מַתַּ֣ת יָד֑וֹ וְשֶׁ֖מֶן הִ֥ין לָאֵיפָֽה׃ס

passages.text: When the prince makes a freewill offering to the LORD, whether a burnt offering or a peace offering, the gate facing east must be opened for him. He is to offer his burnt offering or peace offering just as he does on the Sabbath day. Then he shall go out, and the gate must be closed after he goes out.
passages.sermon:
The prince is the leader of the people.
The prince may choose to give a freewill offering to the LORD.
He may offer a burnt offering or a peace offering.
The gate that faces east must be opened for the prince.
The prince must offer his burnt offering or peace offering.
He must do this in the same way as he does on the Sabbath day.
After the prince finishes his offering, he must go out.
After he goes out, someone must close the gate.
passages.original: וְכִֽי־ יַעֲשֶׂה֩ הַנָּשִׂ֨יא נְדָבָ֜ה עוֹלָ֣ה אֽוֹ־ שְׁלָמִים֮ נְדָבָ֣ה לַֽיהוָה֒ וּפָ֣תַֽח ל֗וֹ אֶת הַשַּׁ֙עַר֙ הַפֹּנֶ֣ה קָדִ֔ים וְעָשָׂ֤ה אֶת־ עֹֽלָתוֹ֙ וְאֶת־ שְׁלָמָ֔יו כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר יַעֲשֶׂ֖ה בְּי֣וֹם הַשַּׁבָּ֑ת וְיָצָ֛א וְסָגַ֥ר אֶת־ הַשַּׁ֖עַר אַחֲרֵ֥י צֵאתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: And you shall provide an unblemished year-old lamb as a daily burnt offering to the LORD; you are to offer it every morning.
passages.sermon:
You must offer a lamb to the LORD every day.
The lamb must be one year old.
The lamb must have no blemish.
You must offer this lamb as a burnt offering.
You must do this every morning.
passages.original: וְכֶ֨בֶשׂ בֶּן־ שְׁנָת֜וֹ תָּמִ֗ים תַּעֲשֶׂ֥ה עוֹלָ֛ה לַיּ֖וֹם לַֽיהֹוָ֑ה בַּבֹּ֥קֶר בַּבֹּ֖קֶר תַּעֲשֶׂ֥ה אֹתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: You are also to provide with it every morning a grain offering of a sixth of an ephah with a third of a hin of oil to moisten the fine flour—a grain offering to the LORD. This is a permanent statute.
passages.sermon:
You must bring a grain offering every morning.
You must bring this grain offering with the lamb.
You must use one sixth of an ephah of fine flour.
You must add one third of a hin of oil to the flour.
You must use the oil to moisten the flour.
You must give this grain offering to the LORD.
This rule is permanent.
You must do this always.
passages.original: וּמִנְחָה֩ תַעֲשֶׂ֨ה עָלָ֜יו בַּבֹּ֤קֶר בַּבֹּ֙קֶר֙ שִׁשִּׁ֣ית הָֽאֵיפָ֔ה וְשֶׁ֛מֶן שְׁלִישִׁ֥ית הַהִ֖ין לָרֹ֣ס אֶת־ הַסֹּ֑לֶת מִנְחָה֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה חֻקּ֥וֹת עוֹלָ֖ם תָּמִֽיד׃

passages.text: Thus they shall provide the lamb, the grain offering, and the oil every morning as a regular burnt offering.’
passages.sermon:
The priests must offer a lamb every morning.
They must also offer a grain offering every morning.
They must add oil to the grain offering every morning.
They must do this as a regular burnt offering to the LORD.
They must do this every day without fail.
passages.original: וְעָשׂוּ אֶת־ הַכֶּ֧בֶשׂ וְאֶת־ הַמִּנְחָ֛ה וְאֶת־ הַשֶּׁ֖מֶן בַּבֹּ֣קֶר בַּבֹּ֑קֶר עוֹלַ֖ת תָּמִֽיד׃פ

passages.text: This is what the Lord GOD says: ‘If the prince gives a gift to any of his sons as an inheritance, it will belong to his descendants. It will become their property by inheritance.
passages.sermon:
The Lord GOD speaks.
The Lord GOD gives a command.
The prince is the ruler of the people.
If the prince gives a gift to one of his sons,
This gift is part of the prince’s inheritance.
The gift will belong to that son.
The son’s descendants will own it after him.
The gift becomes their property by inheritance.
The inheritance stays in the family line.
passages.original: כֹּה־ אָמַ֞ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהֹוִ֗ה כִּֽי־ יִתֵּ֨ן הַנָּשִׂ֤יא מַתָּנָה֙ לְאִ֣ישׁ מִבָּנָ֔יו נַחֲלָת֥וֹ הִ֖יא לְבָנָ֣יו תִּֽהְיֶ֑ה אֲחֻזָּתָ֥ם הִ֖יא בְּנַחֲלָֽה׃

passages.text: But if he gives a gift from his inheritance to one of his servants, it will belong to that servant until the year of freedom; then it will revert to the prince. His inheritance belongs only to his sons; it shall be theirs.
passages.sermon:
The prince may give a gift from his inheritance to one of his servants.
The servant will own the gift until the year of freedom.
After the year of freedom, the gift will return to the prince.
The prince’s inheritance belongs only to his sons.
His sons will receive it as their own.
passages.original: וְכִֽי־ יִתֵּ֨ן מַתָּנָ֜ה מִנַּחֲלָת֗וֹ לְאַחַד֙ מֵֽעֲבָדָ֔יו וְהָ֤יְתָה לּוֹ֙ עַד־ שְׁנַ֣ת הַדְּר֔וֹר וְשָׁבַ֖ת לַנָּשִׂ֑יא אַ֚ךְ נַחֲלָת֔וֹ בָּנָ֖יו לָהֶ֥ם תִּהְיֶֽה׃

passages.text: The prince must not take any of the inheritance of the people by evicting them from their property. He is to provide an inheritance for his sons from his own property, so that none of My people will be displaced from his property.’ ”
passages.sermon:
The prince is the ruler of the people.
The prince must not take the inheritance of the people.
He must not evict anyone from their property.
The prince must give his own property as an inheritance to his sons.
He must not take property from the people for his sons.
This will keep every person in Israel on his own land.
No one among My people will be forced to leave his property.
passages.original: וְלֹא־ יִקַּ֨ח הַנָּשִׂ֜יא מִנַּחֲלַ֣ת הָעָ֗ם לְהֽוֹנֹתָם֙ מֵאֲחֻזָּתָ֔ם מֵאֲחֻזָּת֖וֹ יַנְחִ֣ל אֶת־ בָּנָ֑יו לְמַ֙עַן֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹֽא־ יָפֻ֣צוּ עַמִּ֔י אִ֖ישׁ מֵאֲחֻזָּתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Then the man brought me through the entrance at the side of the gate into the holy chambers facing north, which belonged to the priests, and he showed me a place there at the far western end and said to me, “This is the place where the priests shall boil the guilt offering and the sin offering, and where they shall bake the grain offering, so that they do not bring them into the outer court and transmit holiness to the people.”
passages.sermon:
A man led me.
He brought me through an entrance at the side of the gate.
This entrance led into the holy chambers.
These chambers faced north.
The priests owned these chambers.
He showed me a place at the far western end of the chambers.
He spoke to me.
He said, “This is the place for the priests.
Here the priests will boil the guilt offering.
Here the priests will boil the sin offering.
Here the priests will bake the grain offering.
They will do this here.
They will not bring these offerings into the outer court.
This prevents the people from becoming holy by contact.”
passages.original: וַיְבִיאֵ֣נִי בַמָּבוֹא֮ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עַל־ כֶּ֣תֶף הַשַּׁעַר֒ אֶל־ הַלִּשְׁכ֤וֹת הַקֹּ֙דֶשׁ֙ אֶל־ הַכֹּ֣הֲנִ֔ים הַפֹּנ֖וֹת צָפ֑וֹנָה וְהִנֵּה־ שָׁ֣ם מָק֔וֹם בַּיַּרְכֹתִם יָֽמָּה׃ס וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֔י זֶ֣ה הַמָּק֗וֹם אֲשֶׁ֤ר יְבַשְּׁלוּ־ שָׁם֙ הַכֹּ֣הֲנִ֔ים אֶת־ הָאָשָׁ֖ם וְאֶת־ הַחַטָּ֑את אֲשֶׁ֤ר יֹאפוּ֙ אֶת־ הַמִּנְחָ֔ה לְבִלְתִּ֥י הוֹצִ֛יא אֶל־ הֶחָצֵ֥ר הַחִֽיצוֹנָ֖ה לְקַדֵּ֥שׁ אֶת־ הָעָֽם׃

passages.text: Then he brought me into the outer court and led me around to its four corners, and I saw a separate court in each of its corners.
passages.sermon:
A man guided me.
He brought me into the outer court.
He led me to the four corners of the court.
I looked at each corner.
I saw a separate court in each corner.
passages.original: וַיּוֹצִיאֵ֗נִי אֶל־ הֶֽחָצֵר֙ הַחִ֣יצֹנָ֔ה וַיַּ֣עֲבִירֵ֔נִי אֶל־ אַרְבַּ֖עַת מִקְצוֹעֵ֣י הֶחָצֵ֑ר וְהִנֵּ֤ה חָצֵר֙ בְּמִקְצֹ֣עַ הֶחָצֵ֔ר חָצֵ֖ר בְּמִקְצֹ֥עַ הֶחָצֵֽר׃

passages.text: In the four corners of the outer court there were enclosed courts, each forty cubits long and thirty cubits wide. Each of the four corner areas had the same dimensions.
passages.sermon:
The outer court had four corners.
Each corner had an enclosed court.
Each enclosed court was forty cubits long.
Each enclosed court was thirty cubits wide.
All four enclosed courts had the same size.
All four enclosed courts had the same shape.
passages.original: בְּאַרְבַּ֜עַת מִקְצֹע֤וֹת הֶֽחָצֵר֙ חֲצֵר֣וֹת קְטֻר֔וֹת אַרְבָּעִ֣ים אֹ֔רֶךְ וּשְׁלֹשִׁ֖ים רֹ֑חַב מִדָּ֣ה אַחַ֔ת לְאַרְבַּעְתָּ֖ם מְׄהֻׄקְׄצָׄעֽׄוֹׄתׄ׃

passages.text: Around the inside of each of the four courts was a row of masonry with ovens built at the base of the walls on all sides.
passages.sermon:
There were four courts in the outer court.
Each court had walls around it.
Inside each court, there was a row of masonry along the walls.
Builders placed ovens at the base of these walls.
The ovens were on all sides inside each court.
passages.original: וְט֨וּר סָבִ֥יב בָּהֶ֛ם סָבִ֖יב לְאַרְבַּעְתָּ֑ם וּמְבַשְּׁל֣וֹת עָשׂ֔וּי מִתַּ֥חַת הַטִּיר֖וֹת סָבִֽיב׃

passages.text: And he said to me, “These are the kitchens where those who minister at the temple will cook the sacrifices offered by the people.”
passages.sermon:
A man spoke to me.
He showed me some rooms.
He said, “These rooms are kitchens.”
The kitchens are for those who serve in the temple.
The temple servants will cook here.
They will cook the sacrifices.
The people bring these sacrifices.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אֵלָ֑י אֵ֚לֶּה בֵּ֣ית הַֽמְבַשְּׁלִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֧ר יְבַשְּׁלוּ־ שָׁ֛ם מְשָׁרְתֵ֥י הַבַּ֖יִת אֶת־ זֶ֥בַח הָעָֽם׃
